description: A map is one flat sorted array (Heap::map_put_entry, runtime/src/heap/imp.rs): every put allocates a new array of all entries, so building an n-key map costs n^2/2 entry copies. Measured, release, put 1..n then update 1..n: 10,000 keys 0.66 s, 20,000 2.6 s, 40,000 10.2 s, 80,000 40.6 s; Elixir 0.23-0.28 s throughout (probe: scratchpad/map/mp.exs). The distiller's span table has 23,154 keys on the user's full compile log and is written about three times per key; map put is 10% of the 32,000-line profile and cheney_trace_map 16%. BEAM uses a flat map up to 32 keys and a hash tree above. Tied to the open question of map iteration order past 32 keys. Needs a proposal page.
title: A put into a large map copies a path, not the map
